newsitem.title: USA: Bulgaria debt prices surge as Ecuador Bradys sink.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria debt prices surge as Ecuador Bradys sink.

text.p: The two highest yielding instruments in the emerging debt markets diverged today as Bulgaria continued to celebrate the success of a month-long protest that resulted in a call for early elections and Ecuador began a 48-hour general strike.

"If anything the situation in Bulgaria has turned for the better and the situation in Ecuador has turned the opposite so people are moving out of Ecuador and into Bulgaria which is looking better today," said Tulio Vera, managing director and head of sovereign research at Bear Stearns & Co.

Earlier today, an official from the International Monetary Fund told Reuters in Sofia, that the IMF would resume talks on crucial aid to pull Bulgaria back from the brink of debt defualt as soon as an intereim government was in place.
Meanwhile, political pressures in Ecuador mounted as the country began a general strike to protest government austerity measures and to call for the resignation of President Abdala Bucaram.
At 1630 EST/2130 GMT, Bulgarian discounts BGFLTH24A=RR were 2-1/4 higher at 58 bid and its FLRBs BGFLIRB=RR were 1-1/2 firmer at 40-3/8 bid. The country's IABs BGFLTH11=RR were 7/8 higher at 53 bid.
In contrast, Ecuadorean discounts ECDISC=RR were 1/2 weaker at 69-1/2 bid and its PDIs ECPDI=RR were 1-1/8 lower at 62 bid.
Emerging market sources attributed the rise in Bulgarian debt price to hopes that the economic crisis in Bulgaria can now be averted.

"The sitution is very touch and go. It is very complicated. Indications are that it's very tense, and in my opinion, I think there is more downside than upside in Ecuador," Vera said, notine the increased uncertainty amid the extreme negative sentiment between the Bucaram and the country's Congress.
In Quito earlier, the Speaker of Ecuador's Congress Fabian Alarcon said he had recieved threats that Congress would be dissolved if deputies met to discuss deposing Bucaram.

"I think if anything the fundamental picture looks more complicated because there were some expectations that there would be some measures put to Congress that would improve the economic outlook, particularly fiscal, labor market and fianncial sector reform, and if anything those are most likely going to fall by the wayside now," another source added.
Indeed, market experts are becoming more cautious about Ecuador's economic prospects.

On Tuesday, BankBoston Corp revised it recommended debt allocation weighting to neutral from overweight amid the country's mounting difficulty in achieving convertability, which would peg the currency at four sucres to the dollar.
In the broader sector of the market, sources said prices were mostly lower with U.S. Treasuries.
Argentine pars AR4C23=RR were 3/4 lower at 66 bid, Brazil "C" bonds BR8D14=RR were 5/8 weaker at 78-7/8 bid and Mexico discounts MXFLL19=RR were 1/4 softer at 91-1/8 bid.
